title: Inaudible sounds used to fingerprint browsers catch AliExpress red-handed
gist: A researcher discovered AliExpress running an obsolete WebAudio fingerprinting technique only because it silently hijacked his multipoint Bluetooth headphones' audio routing. The technique no longer works in Firefox, Chrome, or likely Safari — all now ship their own math libraries — but AliExpress runs more than a dozen other fingerprinting methods alongside it, and the author's read is that thousands of sites do the same in an ongoing arms race between browser makers and publishers.

themes.theme: Discovery through an unintended side effect

insights.claim: Researcher Matthew Callaghan found AliExpress's stealth fingerprinting only by accident: loading the AliExpress homepage silenced his phone's audio on multipoint Bluetooth headphones set to defer to PC audio, and closing the tab restored it.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Covert tracking gets exposed by physical-world side effects rather than by audits — device interoperability quirks are an underrated detection channel.
insights.quote: Each time he loaded AliExpress, the phone audio stopped. Each time he closed the tab the site was loaded into, the phone was once again audible.
insights.locator: Researcher Matthew Callaghan said he stumbled

insights.claim: The scripts set audio gain to zero so users hear nothing, but because the audio graph remains connected to the selected system audio device, the browser keeps processing it and eventually transmits the reading back to AliExpress.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Silence is not absence — a zero-gain audio graph still claims the system audio device, which is exactly what made the technique detectable.
insights.quote: The scripts set the gain to zero to prevent users from hearing anything.
insights.locator: The scripts set the gain to zero

insights.claim: Two highly obfuscated scripts render an audio graph that acts as an oscillator generating sawtooth waves, with an analyser measuring the result after it passes through the browser's audio implementation and reading frequency data from it.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The mechanism is measuring floating-point implementation differences, not capturing sound — a reminder that fingerprinting exploits computation, not content.
insights.quote: The analyser measures the result after it has passed through the browser’s audio implementation, and the script reads frequency data from it.

themes.theme: Browser countermeasures have already closed this vector

insights.claim: Audio soundprinting worked because variability in the math libraries browsers used, combined with CPU and system differences, produced a very large number of unique signatures.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Entropy came from OS-supplied library diversity — the general lesson is that any OS-dependent computation is a latent fingerprinting surface.

insights.claim: Firefox killed the technique starting with version 118 in 2023 by shipping its own math libraries instead of relying on those from the host OS, which a Firefox developer says reduced entropy enough to stop it working.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Constant-library bundling is the proven mitigation pattern, and it is now the template other engines follow.
insights.locator: After the audio soundprinting technique became well known

insights.claim: The technique is ineffective in Chrome because it also ships its own libraries per a Google spokesperson, and Safari users are likely safe for the same reason, though Apple did not immediately confirm.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: All major engines are effectively immune, so this specific vector carries no live user risk — the story's value is in what it reveals about the rest of the stack.
insights.locator: The technique is ineffective in Chrome

insights.claim: AliExpress is running more than a dozen other fingerprinting methods alongside the obsolete audio trick, including canvas rendering and toDataURL(), WebGL renderer information and shader precision, screen and viewport dimensions, device pixel ratio, hardware concurrency and device memory, installed plugins, WebRTC behavior, browser performance timing, mouse/touch/focus/scroll events, and device motion and orientation.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Defeating one vector is near-worthless against a dozen-signal composite — anti-fingerprinting has to be evaluated at the stack level.
insights.locator: Callaghan said the other techniques included

insights.claim: AliExpress also probes for properties commonly associated with browser automation, meaning the same script serves bot detection as well as user tracking.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Dual-use framing — fraud prevention — is the defense publishers use to justify fingerprinting stacks against privacy regulation.
insights.quote: properties commonly associated with browser automation
insights.locator: Callaghan said the other techniques included

insights.claim: The author's likely explanation for why AliExpress still runs a broken technique is simply that it is leftover code from years earlier that no one noticed until now.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Tracking stacks accrete rather than get pruned, so observed technique inventories overstate what a site can actually resolve today.
insights.quote: It’s likely the web audio trick is left over from years earlier and no one noticed it until now.

insights.claim: It is almost a certainty that thousands of sites employ similar tracking, and it is not yet clear how effective the rest of AliExpress's metrics are.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Treat this as an industry-wide baseline rather than a single-company scandal — no enforcement action against one retailer changes the aggregate exposure.
insights.quote: it’s almost a certainty that thousands of sites are employing similar tracking
insights.locator: It’s comforting to know that browser makers

insights.claim: Browser developers are in a dynamic race with site publishers who are constantly looking for new ways to break the latest protections.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Privacy protections are perishable by design, so a browser's anti-fingerprinting posture is a maintenance commitment rather than a one-time feature.
insights.quote: Browser developers are in a dynamic race with site publishers, who are constantly looking for new ways to break the latest protections.
